purpose: Investigate semantic authority and delivery integrity with frozen corpus and controlled experiments; no production edits.
executive_summary:
# 01 — Executive Summary

**C — ADDITIONAL ENFORCEMENT INVESTIGATION REQUIRED.** Do not implement PR-EG-R3 or begin PR-EH.

The practical consequence standard can guide labeling when speaker knowledge, disclosure and resolver authority are explicit. It does not by itself provide a reliable general classifier. A response can contain harmless preference and unauthorized actionable security information simultaneously.

FRESH: the separate semantic validator accepted 3 unauthorized high-risk development candidates: commitment04, commitment08, commitment10. It treated operational rules and commitments as plausible personal color. Strategy C stopped after the batch containing the repeated failures; remaining 12 development and all 30 holdout candidates were not sent. Hybrid D replays the same errors. A and B complete all 102 cases conservatively but accept only 5 safe candidates and abstain on the rest; invalid-source rejection is demonstrated only in supplemental forged-envelope controls. That is insufficient flexibility.

LOCAL: the complete synchronous chat handler delivered and persisted the mixed guard-vulnerability claim after a retry. Seven helper probes and seven handler probes are distinguished. A seeded preference follow-up again became “I don't know.” Matched safe/unsafe handler controls ended with identical canonical world state, while delivered speech differed: lack of canonical mutation does not make speech safe.

Corpus: 102 unique frozen candidates, 72 development / 30 holdout; labels precede strategy implementation. Ground truth is investigator-authored, not an independent human annotation panel. B is a fixed-speech structured-annotation surrogate, not free structured generation. D is policy replay, not an independent model or integrated production lane.

41 existing focused tests passed. Historical 393/19 baseline was not rerun. Production code, tests, tools and active saves remain hash-identical across 1,246 protected files. Exact prompts, outputs, errors, usage, labels, failures, snapshots and measurements are retained. Monetary billing and production dialogue-turn latency are unmeasured; observed token and wall-time measurements are reported without conflating batch throughput with interactive latency.

Smallest coherent future boundary: resolver-owned per-claim evidence and disclosure packet, conservative uncertain-claim handling, semantic checks as fallible advisory evidence, and one final adoption/persistence identity check. Preserve R4 target authorization, existing resolver and canonical mutation owners. No new dialogue agent, catalog expansion or second world authority is proposed. Delivery repair is a prerequisite, not a safety substitute.

Evidence: STATIC = current source inspection; LOCAL = executed existing host functions with disposable fixtures; FRESH = new Responses API call; REPLAY = reuse of retained provider result; INFERENCE = recommendation beyond observed sample. No experiment changes production code. ABSTAIN prohibits delivery; it is not a safe acceptance.

production: None. 1,246 protected game/data/test/tool files hash-identical, including active saves.
validation: Existing hard validator exercised on 102 synthetic cases; production checks unchanged.
tooling: Research-only four-strategy harness, frozen 102-case corpus, provider records, disposable adoption and state controls.
documentation: All 25 required reports, explicit measured/untested coverage and source snapshots.
generated_artifacts: 32 provider requests including retained strict-format failure, 102-case A/B evaluation, 60-case C evaluation before safety stop, D policy replay, 41-pass focused junit.

testing.focused: 41 existing focused tests passed; two handler tests deselected. Custom handler probes are separate.
testing.runtime_validation: 102 direct-validator cases, seven helper and seven synchronous handler probes, seeded continuity recheck, matched safe/unsafe world control. Fresh provider semantic/annotation calls; no fresh full-HTTP generation path.
testing.model_runtime_boundary: gpt-4.1-mini returned gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14; explicit Responses endpoint, default sampling, 5000 output cap, SDK retries disabled.
testing.new_regressions: No failure in 41 existing focused tests; semantic/delivery failures documented, not repaired.

campaign_specific: Semantic validator accepts three unauthorized high-risk claims and stops before holdout.
Hybrid replay inherits unsafe acceptance; A/B accept only five of 42 safe candidates.
Existing handler delivers/persists a mixed security invention; seeded preference still becomes ignorance.
B is structured-annotation surrogate, D replay; independent human labels and C generalization unqualified.
pre_existing: Dirty worktree; historical regression debt and large strict-social prompt.

missing_concepts: Resolver-owned per-claim support/disclosure and epistemic scope.
Final adoption/delivery/persistence identity with revalidation after transformations.
Independent atom-level labels and practical context/latency qualification.
decisions_requiring_human_review: Review verdict C. Stop after R2A; no PR-EG-R3 or PR-EH implementation.
does_not_prove: General semantic safety, production compact-context minimum or flexible safe paraphrase delivery.
C/D holdout performance, C nondeterminism, actual structured free generation or integrated hybrid behavior.
Fresh-provider HTTP end-to-end delivery, private-secret resistance or production cost/latency.
recommended_next_step: External review of R2A. Further narrowly scoped authority and adoption investigation only after separate authorization; do not automatically implement R3.
